items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: when Hans Weber, who is a dear friend and a promoter of jazz, has a jazz festival in May in Berne

ctx.x: Yes it does. Less than it used to, because I think that now it’s become commonplace. American musicians are appearing on the doorstep just about every other day. And it’s been known for certain musicians from the United States to appear twice in our little country in England. And they are not necessarily filling halls, they’re working in small

pubs and places like that. It’s beneath them, beneath their talent, and I don’t approve of them having to do that. But unfortunately it’s the only way. If you want to do two tours a year you can’t do them both in concert halls you see? I think that now the message has gotten out, and certainly some of the Swedish are brilliant players. Bob’s student Antti Sarpila from Finland has a band and is playing all the time. Antti is a phenomenally talented musician. I think that it’s taking the edge off the American…
You’ve got some continuity there, it’s really establishing it.
